proposal.title: Mibteshvak: a crawler that preserves interactive pages
proposal.summary: Mibteshvak builds a crawler that preserves interactive pages for libraries and archives.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Interactive pages disappear from archives because crawlers cannot capture them. Libraries and archives depend on web archiving every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a crawler that preserves interactive pages called Mibteshvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Web archiving is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/mibteshvak/mibteshvak, which 21411 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on web archiving for 4 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/mibteshvak/mibteshvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 62000.00 EUR for 100 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 700.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Interactive pages disappear from archives because crawlers cannot capture them. Libraries and archives depend on web archiving every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a crawler that preserves interactive pages called Mibteshvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Web archiving is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/mibteshvak/mibteshvak, which 21411 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on web archiving for 4 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/mibteshvak/mibteshvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
